claims.subject: vp20_parikshit_abhimanyu
claims.summary: Parāśara predicts that Parīkṣit will have Janamejaya as one of four sons.
claims.speaker: Parāśara
claims.note: The four sons are already represented from Viṣṇu Purāṇa 4.20; the same nodes are reused here for the chapter 21 prediction.

claims.summary: In the ANU translation, Śatānīka is described as another son of Parīkṣit.

search_log.query: Viṣṇu Purāṇa Book 4 chapters 21–23 ANU Taylor future descendants Parikshit Bṛhadbala Bṛhadratha
search_log.outcome: Read ANU Press chapters 21–23, retaining their future-tense royal lists as predictions. Added 80 new named persons, while reusing the requested Parīkṣit anchor, earlier four sons, and previously represented Magadha ancestors.

search_log.query: Viṣṇu Purāṇa 4.21–23 Sanskrit verse numbering name and genealogy variants
search_log.outcome: Cross-checked the chapter verse sequence and names against the verse-indexed Sanskrit pages. Kept ANU parentage where translation and Sanskrit presentation differ; documented the Śatānīka parentage variation in chapter 21 and name/sequence variants in chapter 22.

notes: This batch contains 80 new nodes across chapters 21–23. It uses the existing `vp20_parikshit_abhimanyu` anchor requested for chapter 21; the four sons already named in chapter 20 are reused rather than redeclared. Chapter 23 similarly reuses the chapter-19 Bṛhadratha, Jarāsandha, Sahadeva and Somapi nodes.
The source frames these lineages as predictions by Parāśara. Every future-succession edge is recorded as a textual prediction, not as independently established history.

ANU chapter 21 translates Śatānīka as another son of Parīkṣit; the verse-indexed Sanskrit 4.21.2 reads Janamejaya’s son will be Śatānīka. The batch follows ANU, records the variant in the claim note, and keeps this Śatānīka distinct from Nakula’s Śatānika and the later Vasudāna-branch Śatānīka.

Chapter 22’s ANU lineage includes Vatsa and places Vatsavyūha after him, while the linked Sanskrit presentation differs in that sequence; ANU forms are retained as the claim authority. Same-name people in separate dynastic lines (including Sahadeva, Suratha, Niramitra, Bṛhadratha, Bṛhatkarman, Senajit, Dharma, Sumati and Ripuṃjaya) receive branch-specific IDs. ANU Niścaknu also differs from the Sanskrit page’s Nicakṣu; the node keeps ANU’s spelling.
No unnamed sons or generic dynastic groups are expanded. Repeated names from earlier batches are referenced by their existing nodes only where the lineage continuity is explicit.
